definition_zh: v. 擦痛，磨破；（因受限或拖延而）恼怒，烦躁
definition_en: to rub a part of the body until it is sore; to become angry or restless under restriction
core_image: 新鞋后跟磨红一块皮
scene: 新鞋把脚后跟磨得生疼。The new shoes chafed his heels.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chafe 指擦痛；句意是新鞋把脚后跟磨得生疼。

senses.title: To rub sore
senses.definition: to rub a part of the body until it becomes painful
senses.definitionCN: 摩擦身体某处直到发疼
senses.example: The strap chafed her shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 带子把她的肩膀磨疼了。
senses.why: Old French chaufer meant to warm by rubbing.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 chaufer 意为摩擦生热。

senses.title: To fret under restraint
senses.definition: to become angry or restless because of a rule, delay or limit
senses.definitionCN: 因规则、拖延或限制而恼怒不安
senses.example: He chafed at the endless meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 他对无休止的会议感到烦躁。
senses.why: The warmth of rubbing became the heat of impatience.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦的热变成了不耐烦的火气。

intro.en: Chafe descends from a Latin verb for making warm, through a French word for rubbing.
intro.cn: chafe 源自拉丁语「使变热」的动词，经法语「摩擦」一词而来。

items.en: Calefacere means to make warm.
items.cn: calefacere 意为使变热。

items.en: Chaufer means to warm or rub.
items.cn: chaufer 意为加热或摩擦。

items.en: English chafe means to warm by rubbing.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 chafe 意为摩擦生热。

items.en: The verb comes to mean to rub sore.
items.cn: 十六世纪转为磨破皮肤之意。

items.en: Chafe also means to fret at restraint.
items.cn: 十八世纪也指因受限而烦躁。

items.en: Both the rubbing and the fretting senses remain.
items.cn: 摩擦与烦躁两义并存至今。

note.en: The look-alike group sits one letter from chafe; the near-meaning group splits rubbing from fretting.
note.cn: 形近组与 chafe 只差一两个字母；近义组把摩擦与烦躁分开。

entries.definition: To make skin sore by rubbing.

normalIntro.en: A word for warming by rubbing ends up meaning both sore skin and short temper.
normalIntro.cn: 一个「摩擦生热」的词，最后兼指磨破皮与火气大。

normal.en: Calefacere means to make warm.
normal.cn: calefacere 意为使变热。

normal.en: Rubbing skin makes it warm and sore.
normal.cn: 摩擦皮肤让它发热发疼。

normal.en: So chafe means to rub sore.
normal.cn: 于是 chafe 意为磨痛。

normal.en: Warmth also rises into temper.
normal.cn: 热度也会升成火气。

normal.en: To chafe at a rule is to fret.
normal.cn: chafe at a rule 就是因规则而烦躁。

abstract.en: Friction turning into irritation.
abstract.cn: 摩擦变成恼怒。

abstract.en: A collar that rubs all day.
abstract.cn: 整天在磨的衣领。

abstract.en: Patience worn thin at the fold.
abstract.cn: 耐心在折痕处被磨薄。

examples.en: The collar chafed his neck all day.
examples.cn: 衣领把他的脖子磨了一整天。

examples.en: She chafed at the slow paperwork.
examples.cn: 她对缓慢的手续感到烦躁。

examples.en: Tight boots cause chafing on long walks.
examples.cn: 紧靴子在长途步行中会磨伤脚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扯肤」——鞋子扯着皮肤，磨得发疼。

root: 拉丁语 calefacere（使热）→ 古法语 chaufer → 英语 chafe

sensesIntro.en: A word for warming by rubbing drifted into soreness and then into impatience.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「摩擦生热」的词先转为磨痛，再转为烦躁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heel turning red under a tight strap
core.cn: 核心意象：紧带子下磨红的脚跟

branches.en: A heel turning red under a strap.
branches.cn: 带子下磨红的脚跟。

branches.en: A collar rubbed thin at the fold.
branches.cn: 折处被磨薄的衣领。

branches.en: A foot tapping under a desk.
branches.cn: 桌下不停敲地的脚。

branches.en: A sigh at the third delay.
branches.cn: 第三次延误时的一声叹气。

branches.en: Heat that starts in the skin and rises to temper.
branches.cn: 起于皮肤、升为火气的热。

intro.en: Chafe carries a Latin root for warmth; the list below adds words of heat, rubbing and irritation.
intro.cn: chafe 含有「热」的拉丁词根；下面列出热、摩擦与恼怒词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin calere is to be warm, facere is to make, and calor is heat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calere 意为温暖，facere 意为使，calor 意为热。

latinEntries.exampleCN: calefacere 经法语产生 chafe。
calor 产生 calorie 与 caloric。
facere 产生 fact 与 factory。

definition_zh: 链条；一连串；连锁店；用链条拴住
definition_en: a line of connected metal rings, a series of connected things, or to fasten something with a chain
core_image: 一个环扣住下一个环，连成不断的一串
scene: 他用一条铁链把大门锁住。A chain held the gate shut.
sceneCN: 这里 chain 指「链条」（第 1 个义项：相连的金属环）；句意是一条铁链把大门锁住。

senses.title: Connected metal rings
senses.definition: a series of metal rings joined together and used for pulling or fastening
senses.definitionCN: 一串相连的金属环，用于拉动或固定
senses.example: The dog was tied with a strong chain.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗被一条结实的链子拴着。
senses.why: The Latin source named a fetter, so linked metal is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指镣铐，因此相连的金属是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: A connected series
senses.definition: a series of things or events in which each one leads to the next
senses.definitionCN: 一环引出一环的一系列事物或事件
senses.example: A chain of small mistakes ruined the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串小错误毁掉了计划。
senses.why: Linked rings look exactly like linked events, so the physical chain becomes a metaphor for a series.
senses.whyCN: 相连的环与相连的事件看起来一样，于是实物的链成了系列的比喻。

senses.title: To fasten with a chain
senses.definition: to tie or lock something with a chain
senses.definitionCN: 用链条把某物系住或锁住
senses.example: They chained the bicycles to the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把自行车锁在栅栏上。
senses.why: Once the object has a name, using it becomes a verb, so to chain means to apply that metal.
senses.whyCN: 物件有了名称，使用它便成了动词，因此 to chain 意为用上那条金属链。

intro.en: Chain goes back to the Latin word for a fetter and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: chain 可追溯到拉丁语中表示镣铐的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Catena named a chain or fetter of linked metal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catena 指相连金属制成的链子或镣铐。

items.en: The small catenella described one link of such a chain.
items.cn: 指小形式 catenella 描述这种链子的一环。

items.en: Old French chaine dropped the middle sound and named the object.
items.cn: 古法语 chaine 省略中间的音，用来指这件物品。

items.en: English chain first names the metal object used to bind.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 chain 先指用来捆缚的金属物件。

items.en: The word extends to chains of events, chain stores and the verb to chain.
items.cn: 词义扩展到事件链、连锁店以及动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chain family, while the meaning group lists other words for a connected series.
note.cn: 形近组沿 chain 词族展开，近义组列出表示相连系列的其他词。

entries.definitionCN: 把事物链接起来的行为

entries.definition: to set free from a chain
a number of similar things in order
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序排列的若干同类事物

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the linked rings into events, shops and the action of locking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子沿着相连的环，走向事件、店铺以及上锁的动作。

normal.en: Picture one ring holding the next: that grip is the whole idea of a chain.
normal.cn: 想象一个环扣住下一个环，这种扣合就是 chain 的全部要点。

normal.en: A chain of events means each event hooks onto the next like a link.
normal.cn: a chain of events 意为每件事像一环那样钩住下一件。

normal.en: Chain store and chain reaction both spread from one starting point through links.
normal.cn: chain store 与 chain reaction 都通过环节从一个起点扩散。

normal.en: In chains means bound, whether by metal or by rules.
normal.cn: in chains 意为受束缚，无论靠金属还是靠规则。

normal.en: To chain a bike is simply to put the object into action as a verb.
normal.cn: to chain a bike 就是把这件物品当作动词来使用。

abstract.en: Picture a row of paper clips hooked one into another.
abstract.cn: 想象一排回形针一个钩住一个。

abstract.en: Picture dominoes falling in a long unbroken line.
abstract.cn: 想象多米诺骨牌排成长长一列接连倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate rattling in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇上了锁的门在风中作响。

examples.en: The bridge hung on two heavy chains.
examples.cn: 这座桥靠两条沉重的铁链悬着。

examples.en: One small delay started a chain of problems.
examples.cn: 一次小小的延误引发了一连串问题。

examples.en: Please chain the gate before you leave.
examples.cn: 离开前请把大门锁上链条。

dict_mnemonic.text: chain 像「缠」：一环缠住一环，便成了一条链。

root: 源自拉丁语 catena（链、镣铐），经古法语 chaine 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The metal object comes first, linked events borrow its shape, and the verb makes the object an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 金属物件义最先出现，相连事件借用它的形状，动词义又把物件变成动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring gripping the next without a break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一环扣一环，中间没有断开。

branches.en: The first sense keeps the literal metal links.
branches.cn: 第一个义项保留字面上的金属环。

branches.en: The second sense moves the links into time and cause.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把环移到时间与因果之中。

branches.en: The verb applies the object to the act of fastening.
branches.cn: 动词义把物件用于拴缚的动作。

branches.en: Both depend on one part holding the next.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一环扣住下一环。

branches.en: Chain store and chain reaction extend the series to business and science.
branches.cn: 连锁店与连锁反应把系列义扩展到商业与科学。

intro.en: Chain forms chained, chaining and unchain, and it combines freely with other nouns.
intro.cn: chain 构成 chained、chaining 与 unchain，并能与其他名词自由组合。

latinIntro.en: Catena and its small form catenella are the Latin nouns behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: catena 及其指小形式 catenella 是该词背后的拉丁语名词。

items.exampleCN: 大门上挂着沉重的铁链。

items.example: The boat was chained to a post.

items.exampleCN: 链接数据可以节省空间。

items.meaning: a chain worn round the neck

latinEntries.exampleCN: catena 变成古法语 chaine。
catenella 指单独一环。

definition_en: a difficult task, a call to compete, or to question something and demand proof
core_image: 有人当面把一件难事推到你面前
scene: 教练把最难的任务写在黑板上。The coach set us a real challenge.
sceneCN: 这里 challenge 指「挑战」（第 1 个义项：困难的、需要应对的任务）；句意是教练给了我们一个真正的挑战。

senses.title: A difficult task
senses.definition: a task that tests one's ability and is hard to complete
senses.definitionCN: 考验能力、难以完成的任务
senses.example: Learning a language is a long challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 学一门语言是一项长期的挑战。
senses.why: The old French word named an accusation, and a hard task also puts a person on trial.
senses.whyCN: 古法语原词指指控，而艰难的任务同样是在考验一个人。

senses.title: A call to compete
senses.definition: an invitation to fight, play or compete with someone
senses.definitionCN: 邀请他人与自己较量、比赛或打斗
senses.example: He accepted the challenge to race.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了赛跑的挑战。
senses.why: An accusation implies a confrontation, so the word naturally came to mean a summons to compete.
senses.whyCN: 指控本身就含对抗意味，因此这个词自然引申为邀人较量。

senses.title: To question something
senses.definition: to question whether something is right, or to invite someone to compete
senses.definitionCN: 对某事是否正确提出疑问，或邀人较量
senses.example: Several members challenged the report.
senses.exampleCN: 几位成员质疑了这份报告。
senses.why: The original legal accusation survives here: to challenge is to demand that a claim be proved.
senses.whyCN: 最初的法律指控在此留存：质疑就是要求把某个说法证明出来。

intro.en: Challenge began as a legal accusation and gradually moved to contests and to difficult tasks.
intro.cn: challenge 最初指法律上的指控，后来逐步转向较量与艰难的任务。

items.en: Calumnia meant a false accusation and gave the word its accusing core.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calumnia 意为诬告，赋予该词指控的内核。

items.en: Old French chalenge named a claim or a formal accusation.
items.cn: 古法语 chalenge 指主张或正式指控。

items.en: English challenge first appears in law, meaning an objection.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 challenge 先出现在法律中，意为异议。

items.en: The word shifts to duels and contests, a call to prove oneself.
items.cn: 十六世纪词义转向决斗与竞赛，即邀人证明自己。

items.en: The sense widens to hard tasks such as exams and new jobs.
items.cn: 词义再扩展到考试、新工作一类艰难任务。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the challenge family, while the meaning group lists tests, obstacles and dares.
note.cn: 形近组沿 challenge 词族展开，近义组列出考验、障碍与激将的说法。

entries.definition: questioned or put to the test
something that shows how good a person is
entries.definitionCN: 检验一个人水平的事物

entries.definition: something that stands in the way
an invitation to do something bold
entries.definitionCN: 邀人做大胆之事的激将

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the accusation to the contest and then to the hard task.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把指控连到较量，再连到艰难任务。

normal.en: A challenge first accuses you of not being able to do it, and then asks you to try.
normal.cn: challenge 先说你未必做得到，接着请你试一试。

normal.en: Rise to the challenge means stand up and meet the test head on.
normal.cn: rise to the challenge 意为站起来正面迎接考验。

normal.en: Challenging work is hard but interesting, and a challenger wants your place.
normal.cn: challenging 的工作难而有趣，challenger 则想取代你的位置。

normal.en: To challenge a decision is to ask whether it is right.
normal.cn: to challenge a decision 就是追问这个决定是否正确。

normal.en: Face a challenge and meet the challenge both put you in front of the same test.
normal.cn: face a challenge 与 meet the challenge 都把你放到同一场考验面前。

abstract.en: Picture a gauntlet thrown down between two people.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手套被扔到两人之间。

abstract.en: Picture a steep wall that must be climbed in one go.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵必须一口气爬上去的高墙。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a meeting to say: prove it.
abstract.cn: 想象会上一只手举起，表示：请拿出证据。

examples.en: The new job is a real challenge for her.
examples.cn: 这份新工作对她来说是真正的挑战。

examples.en: He challenged me to run one more lap.
examples.cn: 他挑战我再跑一圈。

examples.en: No one challenged the chairman's figures.
examples.cn: 没有人质疑主席给出的数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: challenge 里有「喊」的影子：有人当众喊你出来比一比，就是挑战。

root: 源自拉丁语 calumnia（诬告），经古法语 chalenge 进入英语，义从指控转为较量与难题。

sensesIntro.en: The accusation gives the word its bite, the contest sense grows from it, and the verb carries both.
sensesIntro.cn: 指控给这个词以锋芒，较量义由它生长出来，动词则承载两者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a demand placed in front of someone, with the eyes of others watching.
core.cn: 核心意象：当着众人的面把一项要求摆到某人面前。

branches.en: The task sense turns the demand into a test of ability.
branches.cn: 任务义把要求变成对能力的考验。

branches.en: The contest sense keeps the open confrontation.
branches.cn: 较量义保留公开对抗。

branches.en: The verb covers both questioning and inviting.
branches.cn: 动词义同时涵盖质疑与邀战。

branches.en: Both push a person to prove something.
branches.cn: 两者都推动一个人去证明什么。

branches.en: To challenge a decision is the legal sense surviving in daily use.
branches.cn: to challenge a decision 是法律义在日常中的留存。

intro.en: Challenge builds challenging, challenger and unchallenged, and -ing turns it into a common adjective.
intro.cn: challenge 构成 challenging、challenger 与 unchallenged，-ing 使它成为常用形容词。

latinIntro.en: Calumnia, a false accusation, is the Latin noun at the root of the word.
latinIntro.cn: calumnia（诬告）是这个词根部的拉丁语名词。

items.meaning: a hard task or to question

items.example: The rule was challenged in court.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则在法庭上受到质疑。
她的说法没有受到质疑。
calumny 保留了古老的含义。

latinEntries.exampleCN: calumnia 产生古法语 chalenge。
calumniosus 描述诬告者。

definition_en: a room, especially a private one, a hall where a parliament meets, or a closed space inside a body or machine
core_image: 四面围合起来的一个封闭空间
scene: 庭审结束后，法官走进里间换下法袍。The judge retired to a private chamber.
sceneCN: 这里 chamber 指「房间」（第 1 个义项：私密的室内空间）；句意是法官退到一间私人房间。

senses.title: A private room
senses.definition: a room, especially one used for a private or special purpose
senses.definitionCN: 房间，尤指作私密或特殊用途的房间
senses.example: The council met in a small chamber.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在一间小室里开会。
senses.why: The Greek and Latin sources named a vaulted room, so the enclosed space is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语与拉丁语来源都指拱顶的房间，因此封闭空间是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A hall for a parliament
senses.definition: one of the groups or halls that make up a parliament
senses.definitionCN: 组成议会的机构或厅堂之一
senses.example: The upper chamber rejected the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 上院否决了这项议案。
senses.why: A parliament meets in a great enclosed hall, so the room came to name the body that sits in it.
senses.whyCN: 议会在一座巨大的封闭厅堂里开会，于是房间名转而指坐在其中的机构。

senses.title: An enclosed cavity
senses.definition: a closed space inside a machine, a body or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 机器、身体或建筑物内部的封闭空间
senses.example: Water fills the chamber before it is pumped out.
senses.exampleCN: 水先充满腔室，再被抽出。
senses.why: Any enclosed room can be shrunk to a small sealed space, which is exactly the cavity inside a machine or a heart.
senses.whyCN: 任何围合的房间都能缩小成密封的小空间，这正是机器或心脏内部的腔。

intro.en: Chamber goes back to a Greek word for a vaulted space and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: chamber 可追溯到希腊语中表示拱顶空间的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Kamara named anything with a vaulted, curved roof.
items.cn: 希腊语 kamara 指任何带拱形顶的空间。

items.en: Camera named a vaulted room and later any enclosed room.
items.cn: 拉丁语 camera 指拱顶房间，后来泛指封闭的房间。

items.en: Old French chambre kept the sense of a private room.
items.cn: 古法语 chambre 保留私密房间的含义。

items.en: English chamber first names a private room in a house or castle.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 chamber 先指住宅或城堡中的私室。

items.en: The word widens to parliament halls, machine cavities and chamber music.
items.cn: 词义扩展到议会厅、机器腔室与室内乐。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chamber family, while the meaning group lists rooms and enclosed spaces.
note.cn: 形近组沿 chamber 词族展开，近义组列出房间与封闭空间的说法。

entries.definition: a lawyer's office or a judge's room
a woman who cleans hotel rooms

entries.definitionCN: 被分成多个封闭空间的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the four walls and move to parliament and to hollow spaces.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从四面墙出发，走向议会与中空的空间。

normal.en: Four walls and a roof make a chamber: the idea is enclosure.
normal.cn: 四面墙加一个顶就是 chamber：核心意思是围合。

normal.en: A chamber of commerce gathers businesses in one room of influence.
normal.cn: chamber of commerce 把商家聚在同一间有影响力的屋子里。

normal.en: Chamber music was written for small rooms rather than large halls.
normal.cn: chamber music 是为小房间而非大厅写的。

normal.en: Burial chamber and gas chamber keep the plain sense of an enclosed space.
normal.cn: burial chamber 与 gas chamber 保留封闭空间的直白含义。

normal.en: The upper chamber of a parliament is a hall that became a body.
normal.cn: 议会的上院原本是一个厅，后来变成了一个机构。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone room with a curved ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象一间带弧形顶的小石屋。

abstract.en: Picture a long hall where members rise to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一座长厅，成员们起身发言。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed hollow inside an engine block.
abstract.cn: 想象发动机缸体里一处密封的空腔。

examples.en: The king received them in his private chamber.
examples.cn: 国王在自己的私室里接见了他们。

examples.en: The bill passed the lower chamber easily.
examples.cn: 这项议案在下院顺利通过。

examples.en: The heart has four chambers.
examples.cn: 心脏有四个腔室。

dict_mnemonic.text: chamber 与 camera 同源：最初都指「拱顶的房间」，一个成了室，一个成了相机暗箱。

root: 源自希腊语 kamara（拱顶空间），经拉丁语 camera 与古法语 chambre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A private room comes first, a parliament hall grows from it, and a sealed cavity extends the shape inward.
sensesIntro.cn: 私室义最先出现，议会厅义由它生长，封闭腔室义则把形状向内延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a space closed in by walls on every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面被墙围合起来的空间。

branches.en: The room sense keeps the plain enclosed space.
branches.cn: 房间义保留朴素的封闭空间。

branches.en: The parliament sense turns the hall into an institution.
branches.cn: 议院义把厅堂变成机构。

branches.en: The cavity sense shrinks the room into a hollow inside.
branches.cn: 腔室义把房间缩小成内部空腔。

branches.en: Both rest on a space built for people to gather.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在为人聚集而造的空间上。

branches.en: Room and cavity share the same enclosed shape.
branches.cn: 房间与腔室共享同一种围合形状。

intro.en: Chamber builds chambers, chambermaid and chambered, and it appears in many fixed compounds.
intro.cn: chamber 构成 chambers、chambermaid 与 chambered，并出现在许多固定复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin camera, a vaulted room, is the direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 camera（拱顶房间）是这个英语词的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 客房女服务员换了床单。

items.example: Chambre carried the word to English.

items.meaning: an officer of a royal household

latinEntries.exampleCN: camera 变成古法语 chambre。
camara 保留了弧形的含义。

definition_en: a small tree lizard that can change colour; a person who changes views to suit the moment
core_image: 枝头一只两眼各自转动的蜥蜴
scene: 叶间那只变色龙慢慢变成一片绿。The chameleon slowly turned green among the leaves.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chameleon 指变色龙；句意是叶间的变色龙慢慢变成绿色。

senses.title: The colour-changing lizard
senses.definition: a tree lizard able to change the colour of its skin
senses.definitionCN: 能改变皮肤颜色的树栖蜥蜴
senses.example: A chameleon can move each eye alone.
senses.exampleCN: 变色龙可以单独转动两只眼睛。
senses.why: Greek khamai means on the ground and leon means lion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 khamai 意为地上，leon 意为狮子。

senses.title: A changeable person
senses.definition: someone who shifts views or manner to fit the company
senses.definitionCN: 随场合改变观点或举止的人
senses.example: He is a chameleon in every negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每场谈判里都像变色龙。
senses.why: The colour change became a figure for shifting opinion.
senses.whyCN: 变色成了立场摇摆的比喻。

intro.en: Greek khamaileon joins khamai, on the ground, with leon, a lion.
intro.cn: 希腊语 khamaileon 由 khamai（地上）与 leon（狮子）组合而成。

items.en: Khamai means on the ground.
items.cn: khamai 意为在地面。

items.en: Leon means lion.
items.cn: leon 意为狮子。

items.en: Khamaileon names a ground lion.
items.cn: khamaileon 指地上的狮子。

items.en: Latin keeps the name for the lizard.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用此名指这种蜥蜴。

items.en: English borrows chameleon from Latin.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语从拉丁语借入。

items.en: The word also names a changeable person.
items.cn: 现代也指善变的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cham- sound; the near-meaning group lists other lizards.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cham- 的读音；近义组列出其他蜥蜴。

entries.definition: Soft leather from a mountain goat.

normalIntro.en: A ground lion whose skin takes the colour of the leaves.
normalIntro.cn: 一只皮肤随叶子取色的「地上狮子」。

normal.en: Khamai means on the ground.
normal.cn: khamai 意为在地面。

normal.en: Leon means lion.
normal.cn: leon 意为狮子。

normal.en: A chameleon is a small ground lion.
normal.cn: chameleon 就是小小的地上狮子。

normal.en: Its skin copies the leaves.
normal.cn: 它的皮肤照着叶子取色。

normal.en: A person who copies the room is also a chameleon.
normal.cn: 随场合变色的人也叫 chameleon。

abstract.en: A body that borrows its colour.
abstract.cn: 借用周围颜色的身体。

abstract.en: Two eyes moving in different directions.
abstract.cn: 朝不同方向转动的两只眼。

abstract.en: A self made of the room around it.
abstract.cn: 由周围环境构成的自我。

examples.en: The chameleon matched the leaf exactly.
examples.cn: 那只变色龙与叶子颜色完全一致。

examples.en: Chameleons hunt with a long tongue.
examples.cn: 变色龙用长舌捕猎。

examples.en: Critics called the minister a chameleon.
examples.cn: 批评者称这位部长是变色龙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡米丽恩」——卡在米色叶间，颜色迷离难辨。

root: 希腊语 khamai（地上）+ leon（狮子）→ 拉丁语 chamaeleon → 英语 chameleon

sensesIntro.en: One name for the lizard became a name for the person who mimics the room.
sensesIntro.cn: 蜥蜴的名字又成了模仿周围之人的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coiled tail on a twig and two eyes turning apart
core.cn: 核心意象：细枝上盘起的尾巴与朝两边转动的眼睛

branches.en: A tail coiled around a twig.
branches.cn: 盘在细枝上的尾巴。

branches.en: One eye turned back, one ahead.
branches.cn: 一只眼看后，一只眼看前。

branches.en: A handshake that fits every room.
branches.cn: 在任何场合都合适的握手。

branches.en: A vote that follows the crowd.
branches.cn: 跟着人群走的投票。

branches.en: Skin that takes the colour of the moment.
branches.cn: 随当下取色的皮肤。

intro.en: Chameleon is built from Greek parts; the list below adds words of colour, change and disguise.
intro.cn: chameleon 由希腊语构件组成；下面列出颜色、变化与伪装词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek khamai is on the ground, chroma is colour and Latin mutare is to change.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 khamai 意为在地上，chroma 意为颜色，拉丁语 mutare 意为改变。

latinEntries.exampleCN: chamaeleon 产生英语 chameleon。

latinEntries.example: Khamai is the first half of chameleon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: khamai 是 chameleon 的前半。
chroma 产生 chromatic 与 chromosome。

definition_en: a person or team that has won a competition, or someone who publicly defends a person or cause
core_image: 站在领奖台最高处、把奖杯举过头顶的人
scene: 决赛终场哨响，全场观众起立欢呼。The young boxer became champion after twelve hard rounds.
sceneCN: 这里 champion 指「冠军」（第 1 个义项：比赛中击败所有对手的人）；句意是这位年轻拳手在十二个艰苦回合后成为冠军。

senses.title: The winner of a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that has defeated all rivals in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中击败所有对手的个人或队伍
senses.example: She was champion three years running.
senses.exampleCN: 她连续三年夺得冠军。
senses.why: The Latin base named an open field, and the fighter who won there took the name of the ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基指开阔的场地，在那里取胜的斗士便借用了场地的名字。

senses.title: A defender of a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks or fights publicly for another person or for a principle
senses.definitionCN: 公开为他人或某种原则发声、抗争的人
senses.example: He became a champion of free speech.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了言论自由的捍卫者。
senses.why: The victor who fought for a helpless client lent the word its protecting sense.
senses.whyCN: 为无助者出战的胜者，把「保护」的含义借给了这个词。

senses.title: To support publicly
senses.definition: to defend or promote a person, idea or policy in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合为某人、某观念或某政策辩护或推动
senses.example: The actor championed the small theatre for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这位演员为那家小剧院呼吁了几十年。
senses.why: Once a person was called a champion of a cause, the noun naturally turned into a verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 当人被称作某项事业的 champion 之后，这个名词自然转化为表示支持的动词。

intro.en: Champion travelled from the Latin word for a field to the name of the fighter who stood on it.
intro.cn: champion 从拉丁语表示田野的词出发，最终指站在那片场地上决斗的人。

items.en: Campus meant an open field or plain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 campus 意为开阔的田野或平地。

items.en: Campio named the fighter who settled a dispute by single combat.
items.cn: campio 指以单打决斗解决争端的人。

items.en: Champion entered Old French with the tournament sense intact.
items.cn: champion 带着比武大会的含义进入古法语。

items.en: English used champion for a warrior who fought for another man in a trial.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语用 champion 指在审判中替人出战的武士。

items.en: The word now covers sports winners and public defenders of a cause.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖体育冠军与公共事业的捍卫者。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the field root, while the meaning group names people who prevail.
note.cn: 形近组共享「场地」词根，近义组列出最终取胜的人。

entries.definition: an informal word for a champion
a contest held to decide the top player or team
entries.definitionCN: 决出最佳选手或队伍的比赛

entries.definition: the grounds of a school or college
a person who defeats an opponent
someone who comes first in a contest
a person who protects someone or something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the field root, the short form champ and the fixed phrase champion of a cause.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「场地」词根、短词 champ 以及固定说法 champion of a cause。

normal.en: Champion keeps the field inside it: campus is the open ground where the duel was fought.
normal.cn: champion 里藏着「场地」：campus 就是当年决斗的开阔地。

normal.en: Shorten the word and you get champ, the shout aimed at a winner.
normal.cn: 把词缩短就得到 champ，正是观众对胜者喊出的短词。

normal.en: The -ion ending marks a person, so a champion is the one who owns the field.
normal.cn: -ion 结尾标记出人，champion 就是占住场地的那个人。

normal.en: A champion of a cause wins arguments rather than medals.
normal.cn: a champion of a cause 赢的是论辩，而不是奖牌。

normal.en: The verb champion takes a cause as its object, as in champion the poor.
normal.cn: 动词 champion 的宾语是事业，如 champion the poor 意为为穷人发声。

abstract.en: Picture a raised fist and a silver cup held above a cheering crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起的拳头和一只被举过欢呼人群的银杯。

abstract.en: Picture a lone speaker defending a small village against a powerful company.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人独自为小村庄对抗一家大公司。

abstract.en: Picture a referee lifting the winner's arm at the end of a long fight.
abstract.cn: 想象漫长比赛结束时裁判举起胜者的手臂。

examples.en: She became champion at the age of nineteen.
examples.cn: 她十九岁就成为冠军。

examples.en: The champions lifted the cup together.
examples.cn: 冠军们一起举起了奖杯。

examples.en: He championed the rights of migrant workers.
examples.cn: 他为外来工的权利奔走呼吁。

dict_mnemonic.text: champion 里有 camp（营地）：在营地里比到最后的人，就是冠军。

root: 源自拉丁语 campus（田野、场地），经晚期拉丁语 campio（场上决斗者）与古法语 champion 进入英语；与 camp 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A fighter who wins on the field gives the contest sense, and a fighter who stands up for another gives the defending sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 在场上取胜的斗士给出比赛义，替他人出头的斗士给出捍卫义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fighter left standing on the open field.
core.cn: 核心意象：在开阔场地上站到最后的斗士。

branches.en: A cup and a medal mark the contest winner.
branches.cn: 奖杯与奖牌标记出比赛的胜者。

branches.en: The defender sense keeps the idea of fighting for someone.
branches.cn: 捍卫义保留为某人而战的意思。

branches.en: The verb champion turns the defence into an action.
branches.cn: 动词 champion 把这种捍卫变成动作。

branches.en: Both senses centre on a person who prevails.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以最终取胜的人为中心。

branches.en: Public support appears as both noun and verb.
branches.cn: 公开支持既作名词也作动词出现。

intro.en: Champion keeps the -camp- field root across noun, verb and derived forms.
intro.cn: champion 在名词、动词与派生形式之间保留 -camp- 场地词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin campus and campio are the field and the fighter that gave English the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 campus 与 campio 分别是给出英语这个词的场地与斗士。

items.example: The champion waved to the crowd.

items.exampleCN: 他们曾为这项新法律奔走。
她正在为乡村学校发声。

items.meaning: an informal word for a champion

latinEntries.example: Campio passed into French as champion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: campio 进入法语后写作 champion。

latinEntries.example: Campus gave the word its field image.
latinEntries.exampleCN: campus 赋予这个词场地意象。

definition_en: an opportunity to do something, the likelihood that something will happen, or the way events happen without plan
core_image: 骰子在桌面上翻滚，停在哪一面全凭偶然
scene: 云层压得很低，空气里带着湿气。There is a chance of rain before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 chance 指「可能性」（第 2 个义项：某事发生的可能程度）；句意是中午之前有下雨的可能。

senses.title: An opportunity to act
senses.definition: a situation that makes it possible for you to do something you want
senses.definitionCN: 使你有望做成想做之事的情形
senses.example: This is my last chance to qualify.
senses.exampleCN: 这是我获得资格的最后机会。
senses.why: A throw of the dice opened one outcome among many, and an opening for action took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 掷一次骰子会在众多结果中开出一面，行动的口子也就沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: The likelihood of an event
senses.definition: the degree to which something is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度
senses.example: There is little chance of snow tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚下雪的可能性很小。
senses.why: The fall of the dice could be read as the odds of a result, not merely as luck.
senses.whyCN: 骰子的落点可以被读成某个结果的出现几率，而不只是运气。

senses.title: Luck or accident
senses.definition: the way events happen without being planned or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 事情未经计划与控制而发生的状态
senses.example: They met by chance at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站偶然相遇。
senses.why: When dice decide an outcome, people credit the result to accident rather than design.
senses.whyCN: 当骰子决定结果时，人们把结局归为偶然而非安排。

intro.en: Chance began as the Latin word for dice falling, and the falling became luck, likelihood and opportunity.
intro.cn: chance 起初是拉丁语中骰子落下的说法，这一「落下」后来变成运气、几率与机会。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为落下。

items.en: Cadentia named the falling of dice in a game.
items.cn: cadentia 指游戏中骰子的落下。

items.en: Cheance carried the sense of the way dice happened to fall.
items.cn: cheance 带有骰子碰巧落成怎样的意思。

items.en: English chance first meant a game result and then any unplanned event.
items.cn: 英语 chance 先指游戏结果，后指任何未加计划的事。

items.en: The word now covers luck, probability and a favourable opening.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖运气、概率与有利的时机。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- onset, while the meaning group names openings and luck.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 起首音，近义组列出时机与运气。

entries.definition: to sing words over and over
good or bad fortune that comes by accident
entries.definitionCN: 偶然降临的好运或坏运

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the falling dice, the phrase by chance and the pattern chance of doing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用落下的骰子、短语 by chance 以及 chance of doing 的句式。

normal.en: Chance and cadence share the Latin idea of falling, one for dice and one for rhythm.
normal.cn: chance 与 cadence 共享拉丁语「落下」之意，一个指骰子，一个指节拍。

normal.en: By chance is the shortest way to say that no one planned it.
normal.cn: by chance 是「没人安排」最简短的说法。

normal.en: Take a chance means you accept the dice may fall badly.
normal.cn: take a chance 意为接受骰子可能落得很糟。

normal.en: A chance of rain is a probability, not an invitation.
normal.cn: a chance of rain 说的是概率，不是邀请。

normal.en: The plural chances appears in phrases about odds, as in the chances are slim.
normal.cn: 复数 chances 出现在谈几率的说法里，如 the chances are slim。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of dice spinning across a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 想象一对骰子在木桌上旋转。

abstract.en: Picture a door opening for one second and then closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只开了一秒又关上。

abstract.en: Picture two old friends meeting at a crowded station by accident.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老友在拥挤的车站不期而遇。

examples.en: Everyone deserves a fair chance to speak.
examples.cn: 每个人都应有公平发言的机会。

examples.en: The chances of finding the letter are small.
examples.cn: 找到那封信的可能性很小。

examples.en: I came across the shop by chance.
examples.cn: 我偶然发现了这家店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 chance 想成「禅寺」的谐音：在禅寺门口与旧友偶遇，全凭机会与运气。

root: 源自拉丁语 cadere（落下）的派生形式 cadentia（骰子落下），经古法语 cheance 进入英语，词义由「骰子落点」扩展为运气、几率与机会。

sensesIntro.en: Dice that fall without plan give luck first, then the odds of a result, then the opening that result offers.
sensesIntro.cn: 无计划落下的骰子先给出运气，再给出结果的几率，最后给出该结果带来的时机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dice falling and settling on one face.
core.cn: 核心意象：骰子翻滚后停在某一面。

branches.en: A chance to speak is an opening offered by circumstance.
branches.cn: a chance to speak 是环境给出的开口。

branches.en: A chance of rain measures how likely the event is.
branches.cn: a chance of rain 衡量事件发生的可能。

branches.en: Meeting by chance means no one arranged it.
branches.cn: meeting by chance 意为无人安排。

branches.en: Luck and opportunity both depend on the roll.
branches.cn: 运气与机会都取决于那一掷。

branches.en: Probability and accident share the same image of falling.
branches.cn: 概率与偶然共享同一个「落下」意象。

intro.en: Chance keeps the -cad- falling root in chancy and mischance.
intro.cn: chance 在 chancy 与 mischance 中保留 -cad-「落下」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere and cadentia are the falling verb and noun behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 与 cadentia 是英语这个词背后的「落下」动词与名词。

items.exampleCN: 那个计划看起来靠不住。

items.example: By mischance the letter arrived late.
Cadere is the old falling verb.
items.exampleCN: cadere 是古老的「落下」动词。

items.example: Cadentia named a throw of dice.
The occasion called for a speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个场合需要一篇讲话。

latinEntries.example: Cadere is the source of cadence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cadere 是 cadence 的来源。
cadentia 在法语中变成 cheance。

definition_zh: n. （德国、奥地利）总理；财政大臣；（大学）名誉校长；衡平法院法官
definition_en: the head of government in some countries; a senior finance minister; the ceremonial head of a university
core_image: 议会前排一个宣读预算的人
scene: 财政大臣在下议院宣读了预算。The chancellor read the budget to the Commons.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chancellor 指财政大臣；句意是财政大臣向下议院宣读预算。

pos.zh: 总理；财政大臣；大学名誉校长

senses.title: Finance minister or premier
senses.definition: a senior minister in charge of finance, or the head of government in some states
senses.definitionCN: 主管财政的高级大臣，或某些国家的政府首脑
senses.example: The German chancellor opened the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 德国总理宣布峰会开幕。
senses.why: Latin cancellarius was an officer at a lattice screen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cancellarius 是站在格栅后的官员。

senses.title: University head
senses.definition: the ceremonial head of a university
senses.definitionCN: 大学的礼仪性最高负责人
senses.example: The chancellor handed out the degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 名誉校长颁发了学位证书。
senses.why: The office kept its dignity long after its power moved elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 职权转移后，这个职位仍保留尊荣。

intro.en: Chancellor comes from Latin cancellarius, the officer who stood at the lattice rail of a court.
intro.cn: chancellor 来自拉丁语 cancellarius，指站在法庭格栅旁的官员。

items.en: Cancelli are the lattice rails of a court.
items.cn: cancelli 是法庭的格栅栏杆。

items.en: A cancellarius is the officer at the rail.
items.cn: cancellarius 是站在栏杆处的官员。

items.en: The title passes to church officers.
items.cn: 十一世纪该称号传给教会官员。

items.en: England has a chancellor of the exchequer.
items.cn: 十三世纪英格兰设财政大臣。

items.en: The title names a head of government.
items.cn: 十九世纪指政府首脑。

items.en: Universities keep a ceremonial chancellor.
items.cn: 大学保留礼仪性的校长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chancel- shape; the near-meaning group ranks political and academic heads.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chancel- 的形态；近义组排列政治与学术首脑。

entries.definition: The part of a church by the altar.
The staff and office of a chancellor.
A senior member of a government.

normalIntro.en: The man at the rail of the court became the man with the budget.
normalIntro.cn: 站在法庭栏杆边的人，后来成了拿预算的人。

normal.en: Cancelli means a lattice rail.
normal.cn: cancelli 意为格栅栏杆。

normal.en: A cancellarius stood at that rail.
normal.cn: cancellarius 就站在栏杆旁。

normal.en: The office grew into a minister.
normal.cn: 这个职位长成了大臣。

normal.en: In Germany it heads the government.
normal.cn: 在德国它是政府首脑。

normal.en: In a university it is ceremonial.
normal.cn: 在大学里它是礼仪性的。

abstract.en: A red box on a green bench.
abstract.cn: 绿长椅上的红皮箱。

abstract.en: Authority that keeps its old furniture.
abstract.cn: 保留旧家具的权威。

abstract.en: A robe that still opens parliaments.
abstract.cn: 仍为议会开幕的礼袍。

examples.en: The chancellor announced a tax cut.
examples.cn: 财政大臣宣布减税。

examples.en: She became the first woman chancellor.
examples.cn: 她成为第一位女总理。

examples.en: The chancellor shook hands with every graduate.
examples.cn: 名誉校长与每位毕业生握手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「钱塞了」——钱都塞给财政大臣管。

root: 拉丁语 cancelli（格栅）→ cancellarius（栅后官员）→ 英语 chancellor

sensesIntro.en: One Roman office at a lattice rail became both a finance minister and a university figurehead.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个古罗马栅栏旁的职位，后来既是财政大臣也是大学名誉校长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official standing at a lattice rail with a sealed document
core.cn: 核心意象：带着密封文书站在格栅旁的官员

branches.en: A red box carried into the chamber.
branches.cn: 提进议事厅的红皮箱。

branches.en: A budget speech read line by line.
branches.cn: 逐行宣读的预算演说。

branches.en: A robe and a ceremonial mace.
branches.cn: 礼袍与仪仗权杖。

branches.en: A graduate crossing a stage.
branches.cn: 走上台的毕业生。

branches.en: An old title wearing modern power.
branches.cn: 披着现代权力的旧头衔。

intro.en: Chancellor keeps a Latin office in its stem; the list below adds words of office, service and rank.
intro.cn: chancellor 的词干保留了拉丁官职；下面列出官职、服务与等级词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cancelli are lattice rails and minister is a servant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli 意为格栅，minister 意为仆人。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cancelli 产生 chancel 与 chancellor。

latinEntries.example: Cancellarius is the direct source of chancellor.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cancellarius 是 chancellor 的直接来源。
minister 产生 minister 与 ministry。

definition_en: a television or radio station, a passage through which water or information moves, or a narrow stretch of sea
core_image: 一条被水流长期冲出的窄沟
scene: 山谷深处的岩壁被水磨得光滑。The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 channel 指「水道；通道」（第 2 个义项：水或其他事物通过的路径）；句意是河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。

senses.title: A television or radio band
senses.definition: a band of frequencies used by a particular television or radio station
senses.definitionCN: 某家电视台或电台使用的频段
senses.example: Switch to another channel after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻结束后换到另一个频道。
senses.why: Broadcasting needed a word for a path that carries a signal, and the waterway word supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 广播需要一个表示信号通路的词，而水道这个词正好补上。

senses.title: A passage for water or information
senses.definition: a passage through which water, goods or information moves
senses.definitionCN: 水、货物或信息通过的路径
senses.example: The river cut a narrow channel through the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 河水在岩石间冲出一条狭窄的水道。
senses.why: The Latin base meant a pipe or groove, the exact shape of any narrow passage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基意为管道或沟槽，正是任何狭窄通道的形状。

senses.title: A narrow sea passage
senses.definition: a narrow stretch of water between two areas of land
senses.definitionCN: 两片陆地之间的狭长水域
senses.example: Ships waited for calm weather to cross the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 船只等待风平浪静时穿越海峡。
senses.why: A groove filled with sea water is simply the waterway sense on a map-sized scale.
senses.whyCN: 灌满海水的沟槽，不过是水道义在地图尺度上的放大。

intro.en: Channel goes back to a Latin word for a pipe, and every later sense keeps that shape of a narrow passage.
intro.cn: channel 可追溯到拉丁语表示管道的词，后来各义项都保留狭窄通路这一形状。

items.en: Canalis meant a pipe, groove or water channel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 意为管道、沟槽或水道。

items.en: Chanel named a bed of a stream or a narrow sea passage.
items.cn: chanel 指河床或狭窄的海上通道。

items.en: English channel first described a watercourse and a strait.
items.cn: 英语 channel 先描述水道与海峡。

items.en: The word extended to any route by which something travels.
items.cn: 该词扩展到任何事物通行的路线。

items.en: Radio and television gave it the sense of a broadcast band.
items.cn: 广播与电视赋予它播出频段的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the canal shape, while the meaning group lists other passages and routes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 canal 的外形，近义组列出其他通道与路线。

entries.definition: the area around the altar of a church
a way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处的路线

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the canal root, the sea strait and the phrase through official channels.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 canal 词根、海峡义以及短语 through official channels。

normal.en: Channel and canal are twins from the Latin word for a pipe.
normal.cn: channel 与 canal 是拉丁语「管道」一词的双胞胎。

normal.en: A television channel is a groove cut for a signal instead of water.
normal.cn: 电视频道就是为信号而非水流开出的沟。

normal.en: Through official channels means by the proper route, not by a shortcut.
normal.cn: through official channels 意为走正规路线，而非抄近路。

normal.en: The English Channel is simply the waterway sense written on a map.
normal.cn: the English Channel 不过是水道义写在地图上。

normal.en: The verb channel takes resources as its object, as in channel funds into schools.
normal.cn: 动词 channel 以资源为宾语，如 channel funds into schools。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow groove in stone with water running through it.
abstract.cn: 想象石头上一条窄沟，水从中流过。

abstract.en: Picture a remote control clicking from one station to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象遥控器从一个台跳到下一个台。

abstract.en: Picture ships queuing between two headlands in grey weather.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗天气里船只在两处海角间排队。

examples.en: The interview will be shown on channel four.
examples.cn: 这次采访将在第四频道播出。

examples.en: Complaints should go through the proper channels.
examples.cn: 投诉应通过正当渠道提出。

examples.en: They channelled the extra money into research.
examples.cn: 他们把额外的钱投入研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 channel 想成 canal（运河）：运河是水的频道，电视频道是信号的运河。

root: 源自拉丁语 canalis（管道、沟槽），经古法语 chanel 进入英语；与 canal 同源，核心形状是狭长的通路。

sensesIntro.en: A groove for water becomes a passage for goods and news, a strait on the map and a band for broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 流水的沟槽变成货物与消息的通道，再变成地图上的海峡与播出的频段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow groove that carries something along.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把某物往前输送的窄沟。

branches.en: A broadcast band is a channel for a signal.
branches.cn: 播出频段是信号的通道。

branches.en: A river channel is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 河道是最古老也最具体的义项。

branches.en: A strait is a channel at the scale of a map.
branches.cn: 海峡是地图尺度上的通道。

branches.en: Both keep the image of water finding a narrow way.
branches.cn: 两者都保留水寻找窄路的意象。

branches.en: Information now flows where water once flowed.
branches.cn: 如今信息在昔日水流之处流动。

intro.en: Channel keeps the -canal- root in canal, channelization and multichannel.
intro.cn: channel 在 canal、channelization 与 multichannel 中保留 -canal- 词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin canalis is the pipe that gave both channel and canal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 canalis 就是给出 channel 与 canal 的那根管道。

items.example: The channel was full of mud.
They channelled water to the field.
She is channelling her energy into work.
Canalis is the old pipe word.
The tunnel runs under the river.

latinEntries.exampleCN: canalis 在法语中变成 chanel。

latinEntries.example: Canal is the twin of channel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: canal 是 channel 的双胞胎。

definition_en: a state of complete disorder, or the formless void believed to exist before the ordered world
core_image: 所有东西同时散落，找不到任何次序
scene: 停电后路口乱成一团。Traffic fell into chaos after the lights failed.
sceneCN: 这里 chaos 指「混乱」（第 1 个义项：完全失去秩序的状态）；句意是信号灯失灵后交通陷入混乱。

senses.title: Complete disorder
senses.definition: a state in which everything is confused and has no order
senses.definitionCN: 一切事物都杂乱无章、毫无秩序的状态
senses.example: The office was in chaos after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬完之后办公室一片混乱。
senses.why: The Greek word named the void before creation, and any total loss of order recalls that void.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词指创世之前的虚空，任何彻底失序都让人想起那片虚空。

senses.title: The formless state before the world
senses.definition: the empty, formless state that Greek myth placed before the ordered universe
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话置于有序宇宙之前的空虚无形状态
senses.example: Greek myths begin with chaos.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊神话从混沌开始。
senses.why: Hesiod used the word for the gap that opened before earth and sky were separated.
senses.whyCN: 赫西俄德用这个词指大地与天空分开之前张开的空隙。

senses.title: A jumble of unconnected things
senses.definition: a confused mass of objects or ideas with no pattern
senses.definitionCN: 毫无规律地堆在一起的物件或想法
senses.example: The desk was a chaos of papers and cups.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上是一堆杂乱的文件和杯子。
senses.why: A desk that loses every pattern is a small private copy of the original void.
senses.whyCN: 一张失去全部规律的桌子，就是那片原始虚空的小型私人翻版。

intro.en: Chaos is a Greek word for a gap or void, taken into English to name any total disorder.
intro.cn: chaos 是希腊语中表示裂缝或虚空的词，进入英语后指任何彻底的混乱。

items.en: Khaos meant a gap, chasm or empty space.
items.cn: 希腊语 khaos 意为裂缝、深渊或空旷之处。

items.en: Hesiod made Khaos the formless state before the gods.
items.cn: 赫西俄德把 khaos 写成众神之前的无形状态。

items.en: Latin chaos kept the cosmological sense of the void.
items.cn: 拉丁语 chaos 保留了虚空的宇宙论含义。

items.en: English chaos first described the state before creation.
items.cn: 英语 chaos 先描述创世之前的状态。

items.en: The word now also means any messy, uncontrolled situation.
items.cn: 如今该词也指任何杂乱失控的局面。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek stem, while the meaning group lists states of disorder.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊语词干，近义组列出各种失序状态。

entries.definition: a deep opening in the ground
the study of systems that look random
entries.definitionCN: 研究看似随机系统的学问

entries.definition: a state in which things are unclear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek void, the chaotic adjective and the phrase in chaos.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语虚空、形容词 chaotic 以及短语 in chaos。

normal.en: Chaos is the gap before the world, so a chaotic room has lost its order.
normal.cn: chaos 是世界之前的裂缝，所以 chaotic 的房间就是失去了次序。

normal.en: The adjective chaotic adds -ic, and the adverb adds -ally.
normal.cn: 形容词 chaotic 加 -ic，副词再在其后加 -ally。

normal.en: In chaos needs no article, because the noun is uncountable.
normal.cn: in chaos 不加冠词，因为这个词不可数。

normal.en: Chaos theory studies systems whose starting point decides everything.
normal.cn: chaos theory 研究起点决定一切的系统。

normal.en: A chaos of papers describes a heap with no pattern at all.
normal.cn: a chaos of papers 描述完全没有规律的一堆纸。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every drawer has been emptied at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，所有抽屉同时被倒空。

abstract.en: Picture a dark gap opening before the first light.
abstract.cn: 想象第一道光之前张开的黑暗裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a crossroads with dead lights and honking cars.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信号灯全灭、汽车鸣笛的路口。

examples.en: The airport was in chaos after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后机场一片混乱。

examples.en: He tried to bring order to the chaos of his notes.
examples.cn: 他试着把杂乱的笔记理出头绪。

examples.en: The old story says the world rose out of chaos.
examples.cn: 古老的故事说世界从混沌中升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: chaos 读起来像「吵死」：一群人吵得不可开交，场面就是一片混乱。

root: 源自希腊语 khaos（裂缝、虚空），经拉丁语 chaos 进入英语，由「创世前的无形虚空」引申为彻底的混乱。

sensesIntro.en: The empty gap before creation gives the mythic sense first, then any total disorder, then a mere jumble.
sensesIntro.cn: 创世前的空虚先给出神话义，再给出彻底的混乱，最后给出普通的一堆杂物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formless gap where nothing has its place.
core.cn: 核心意象：万物都找不到位置的无形空隙。

branches.en: A chaotic office has lost every pattern.
branches.cn: 混乱的办公室失去了全部规律。

branches.en: Myth places chaos before earth and sky.
branches.cn: 神话把混沌放在天地之前。

branches.en: A heap of papers is chaos on a small scale.
branches.cn: 一堆纸是缩小尺度的混乱。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of no order at all.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「全无秩序」的意思。

branches.en: The everyday mess echoes the cosmic void.
branches.cn: 日常的杂乱呼应着宇宙的虚空。

intro.en: Chaos forms chaotic and chaotically with the adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: chaos 借助形容词与副词词尾构成 chaotic 与 chaotically。

latinIntro.en: The word passed from Greek khaos into Latin chaos before reaching English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从希腊语 khaos 进入拉丁语 chaos，再到英语。

items.meaning: a deep gap in the earth
items.example: A chasm opened in the road.

latinEntries.exampleCN: khaos 出现在众神之前。

latinEntries.example: Latin chaos kept the Greek sense.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 chaos 保留了希腊语义。

definition_zh: n. 小教堂；（学校、医院等建筑内的）祈祷室
definition_en: a small church, or a room used for prayer inside a larger building
core_image: 一排窄长椅与门上一扇彩窗
scene: 村口的小教堂只摆得下六排长椅。The chapel at the village edge held only six rows of pews.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chapel 指小教堂；句意是村口小教堂只容得下六排长椅。

senses.title: Small church
senses.definition: a small building used for Christian worship
senses.definitionCN: 用于基督教礼拜的小型建筑
senses.example: They married in a stone chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一座石头小教堂里结婚。
senses.why: The name comes from the shrine that held a saint cloak.
senses.whyCN: 名称来自存放圣人斗篷的圣龛。

senses.title: Prayer room inside a building
senses.definition: a room set aside for prayer in a school, hospital or airport
senses.definitionCN: 学校、医院或机场里辟出的祈祷室
senses.example: The hospital chapel stays open all night.
senses.exampleCN: 医院祈祷室整夜开放。
senses.why: The small church moved indoors with the institution.
senses.whyCN: 小教堂随机构一起搬进了室内。

intro.en: Chapel descends from cappella, the shrine that held a saint cloak, from Latin cappa, a cloak.
intro.cn: chapel 来自 cappella（存放圣人斗篷的圣龛），源自拉丁语 cappa（斗篷）。

items.en: Cappa means a cloak.
items.cn: cappa 意为斗篷。

items.en: Cappella is the shrine holding a cloak.
items.cn: cappella 是存放斗篷的圣龛。

items.en: Chapele names the shrine and its building.
items.cn: chapele 指圣龛及其建筑。

items.en: English chapel names a small church.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语指小教堂。

items.en: Schools and hospitals add indoor chapels.
items.cn: 十九世纪学校与医院设室内祈祷室。

items.en: The word covers both building and room.
items.cn: 现代兼指建筑与房间。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chapel shape; the near-meaning group ranks places of worship.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chapel 的形态；近义组排列礼拜场所。

entries.definition: A priest who serves an institution.
A small wreath or string of beads.
A small room for private prayer.
A place holding a sacred object.

normalIntro.en: A cloak kept in a shrine gave its name to a small church.
normalIntro.cn: 存于圣龛里的一件斗篷，把名字给了小教堂。

normal.en: Cappa means a cloak.
normal.cn: cappa 意为斗篷。

normal.en: A cappella is the shrine that keeps it.
normal.cn: cappella 是存放它的圣龛。

normal.en: French chapele names the building.
normal.cn: 法语 chapele 指那座建筑。

normal.en: English chapel is a small church.
normal.cn: 英语 chapel 是小教堂。

normal.en: Big buildings keep one indoors.
normal.cn: 大楼里也辟出一间。

abstract.en: A cloak turned into a room.
abstract.cn: 一件斗篷变成一间屋子。

abstract.en: Six rows of silence.
abstract.cn: 六排寂静。

abstract.en: A small light inside a large building.
abstract.cn: 大楼里的一小点光。

examples.en: A candle burned at the back of the chapel.
examples.cn: 小教堂后方点着一支蜡烛。

examples.en: The chapel bells rang at six.
examples.cn: 小教堂的钟在六点敲响。

examples.en: She prayed in the airport chapel.
examples.cn: 她在机场祈祷室祈祷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「查普儿」——查一查谱儿，小教堂里做礼拜。

root: 拉丁语 cappa（斗篷）→ cappella（圣龛）→ 古法语 chapele → 英语 chapel

sensesIntro.en: The shrine that guarded a cloak became the small church, and then the prayer room indoors.
sensesIntro.cn: 存放斗篷的圣龛变成小教堂，再变成室内的祈祷室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny stone room with six rows of pews and one coloured window
core.cn: 核心意象：有六排长椅和一扇彩窗的小石屋

branches.en: Six rows of polished pews.
branches.cn: 六排磨亮的长椅。

branches.en: A single stained window above the door.
branches.cn: 门上方唯一一扇彩窗。

branches.en: A quiet room off a hospital corridor.
branches.cn: 医院走廊旁的静室。

branches.en: A prayer mat folded in an airport corner.
branches.cn: 机场角落里卷起的祈祷垫。

branches.en: A small holy room, standing alone or tucked inside.
branches.cn: 独立或嵌入大建筑的小圣室。

intro.en: Chapel rests on a Latin word for a cloak; the list below adds words of worship and small buildings.
intro.cn: chapel 建于拉丁语「斗篷」一词；下面列出礼拜与小建筑词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cappa is a cloak and sanctus is holy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cappa 意为斗篷，sanctus 意为神圣。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cappa 产生 cape 与 chapel。

latinEntries.example: Cappella is the direct source of chapel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cappella 是 chapel 的直接来源。
sanctus 产生 saint 与 sanctuary。

definition_zh: v. 烧焦，烤焦；（英，旧）做清洁工；n. （英，旧）清洁女工
definition_en: to burn something slightly so that its surface turns black; a British word for a cleaner
core_image: 平底锅里香肠表面焦黑
scene: 香肠在锅里被烤得焦黑。The sausages charred in the pan.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：char 指烤焦；句意是香肠在锅里被烤得焦黑。

senses.title: To burn the surface
senses.definition: to blacken the surface of something with heat
senses.definitionCN: 用高温把某物表面烧黑
senses.example: Char the peppers over an open flame.
senses.exampleCN: 在明火上把辣椒烤焦。
senses.why: The verb is a back-formation from charcoal.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由 charcoal 逆构而来。

senses.title: A cleaner
senses.definition: a British word, now dated, for a person who cleans houses or offices
senses.definitionCN: 英式旧称，指打扫房屋或办公室的人
senses.example: A char came in twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一位清洁工每周来两次。
senses.why: The cleaning sense grew from the idea of turning over work by the day.
senses.whyCN: 清洁义由按日计工的零活引申而来。

intro.en: Char begins in an old word meaning to turn, and the burnt sense comes through charcoal.
intro.cn: char 起于意为「转动」的古词，烧焦义经 charcoal 而来。

items.en: Cerran means to turn.
items.cn: cerran 意为转动。

items.en: Char means to turn or do odd work.
items.cn: 中古英语 char 意为转动或做零活。

items.en: Charcoal gives the verb to char.
items.cn: charcoal 衍生出动词 char。

items.en: To char means to blacken with heat.
items.cn: 十八世纪指用高温烧黑。

items.en: A char is a cleaner paid by the day.
items.cn: 十九世纪指按日付酬的清洁工。

items.en: The cooking sense now leads.
items.cn: 现代以烹饪义为主。

note.en: The look-alike group changes one letter; the near-meaning group ranks degrees of burning.
note.cn: 形近组只差一两个字母；近义组排列烧灼的不同程度。

entries.definition: To damage with fire or heat.

normalIntro.en: Char is the black part of the grill line.
normalIntro.cn: char 就是烤架上那道黑印。

normal.en: Cerran means to turn.
normal.cn: cerran 意为转动。

normal.en: Charcoal is wood turned black.
normal.cn: charcoal 是被烧黑的木头。

normal.en: The verb char comes from it.
normal.cn: 动词 char 由此而来。

normal.en: A flame makes the surface black.
normal.cn: 火把表面烧黑。

normal.en: A char also cleaned houses by the day.
normal.cn: char 还指按日上门的清洁工。

abstract.en: Heat writing in black.
abstract.cn: 用高温写的黑字。

abstract.en: A surface that remembers the flame.
abstract.cn: 记住火焰的表面。

abstract.en: Work that leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 会留下痕迹的活。

examples.en: Char the tomatoes until the skins split.
examples.cn: 把番茄烤到表皮裂开。

examples.en: The toast was charred at the edges.
examples.cn: 吐司边缘烤焦了。

examples.en: The grill left dark char lines on the fish.
examples.cn: 烤架在鱼身上留下黑色的焦痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「茶」——茶壶干烧，壶底烧焦。

root: 中古英语 charren（转动、做零活）→ char；烧焦义与 charcoal 相关

sensesIntro.en: A word for turning work over by the day also names the black mark that heat leaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个指「按日转手零活」的词，也指高温留下的黑印。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black stripes left by a flame on a surface
core.cn: 核心意象：火焰在表面上留下的黑色条纹

branches.en: A pepper blistering on a flame.
branches.cn: 明火上起泡的辣椒。

branches.en: Black stripes on a grilled fish.
branches.cn: 烤鱼上的黑条纹。

branches.en: A bucket and mop in a hallway.
branches.cn: 走廊里的水桶与拖把。

branches.en: An early key turning in an office door.
branches.cn: 清晨转动办公室门锁的钥匙。

branches.en: Work that leaves a mark, on food or on a floor.
branches.cn: 在食物或地板上留下痕迹的活。

intro.en: Char is a native English word; the list below adds words of burning and residue.
intro.cn: char 是英语本族词；下面列出燃烧与残渣词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo is charcoal and cinis is ash.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carbo 意为木炭，cinis 意为灰。

latinEntries.exampleCN: carbo 产生 carbon 与 carbonize。
cinis 产生 cinerary 与 incinerate。

latinEntries.example: Ustus appears in combust and ustulate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ustus 见于 combust 与 ustulate。

definition_en: the qualities that make a person or place distinct, a person in a story, or a letter or symbol used in writing
core_image: 刻在金属上的一枚印记，显示物件的本色
scene: 小说里的老人沉默而固执。The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
sceneCN: 这里 character 指「人物」（第 2 个义项：故事中的人物）；句意是小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。

senses.title: The qualities of a person
senses.definition: the set of qualities that make a person or place what it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某地成为其自身的全部品质
senses.example: She has a strong character.
senses.exampleCN: 她性格坚强。
senses.why: Greek kharakter was the mark stamped on a coin, an outward sign of what lay inside.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kharakter 是压在硬币上的印记，是内在之物的外在标志。

senses.title: A person in a story
senses.definition: a person in a novel, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 小说、戏剧或电影中的人物
senses.example: The old man in the novel is a memorable character.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的这位老人是个令人难忘的人物。
senses.why: Writers borrowed the stamped mark for the figures stamped into a story.
senses.whyCN: 作家把压印的记号借来，指被压进故事里的那些人物。

senses.title: A letter or symbol
senses.definition: a letter, number or symbol used in writing or printing
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷所用的字母、数字或符号
senses.example: The password needs eight characters.
senses.exampleCN: 密码需要八个字符。
senses.why: A stamped mark is literally a written sign, so the alphabet sense is the oldest of all.
senses.whyCN: 压出的印记本就是一种书写符号，所以字符义其实最为古老。

intro.en: Character began as a Greek word for an engraved mark and grew into nature, symbol and story figure.
intro.cn: character 起初是希腊语中「刻痕」的说法，后来生长出本性、符号与故事人物诸义。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark or stamp.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的痕迹或印章。

items.en: The word also named the distinctive stamp of a person's nature.
items.cn: 该词也指一个人本性上独有的印记。

items.en: Latin character kept both the written sign and the moral sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 同时保留书写符号与品格两义。

items.en: English character first meant a written symbol.
items.cn: 英语 character 最初指书写符号。

items.en: The word now covers personality, reputation and people in fiction.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖性格、名声与虚构作品中的人物。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on the same stem, while the meaning group lists nature and symbol words.
note.cn: 形近组由同一词干构成，近义组列出本性词与符号词。

entries.definition: to describe the nature of something
the pattern of a person's behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 一个人行为的整体模式

entries.definition: a person shown in a story or picture
entries.definitionCN: 故事或图画中出现的人物

entries.definition: a sign that stands for something

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the engraved mark, the Chinese character phrase and the story sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用刻痕意象、短语 Chinese character 以及故事人物义。

normal.en: Character and carve share the idea of cutting a mark into a surface.
normal.cn: character 与 carve 共享在表面刻下痕迹的意思。

normal.en: A Chinese character is literally a written mark, the oldest sense of the word.
normal.cn: a Chinese character 本就是一个书写记号，正是这个词最古老的义项。

normal.en: In character means the action fits the mark already stamped on the person.
normal.cn: in character 意为行为符合早已印在那人身上的记号。

normal.en: A main character carries the plot, just as a stamp carries a claim.
normal.cn: main character 承载情节，正如印章承载声明。

normal.en: The plural characters covers letters, people and personal traits at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characters 同时涵盖字符、人物与性格特征。

abstract.en: Picture a hot stamp pressed into soft wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚滚烫的印章压进软蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a novel where one old man keeps returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一部小说里有一位反复出现的老者。

abstract.en: Picture a password box asking for eight signs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密码框要求输入八个符号。

examples.en: The town has a character of its own.
examples.cn: 这座小镇自有其特色。

examples.en: The two characters meet again at the end.
examples.cn: 两个人物在结尾重逢。

examples.en: Write your name in capital characters.
examples.cn: 请用大写字母写你的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: character 与「刻」有关：希腊语原义是刻下的印记，性格就是刻在人身上的记号。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakter（刻痕、印记），经拉丁语 character 进入英语；核心是「刻下的记号」，由此引申出符号、性格与人物。

sensesIntro.en: A stamp makes a written sign, marks a person's nature and presses a figure into a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 一枚印章既留下书写符号，也标记人的本性，还把人物压进故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark cut into a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻进表面的一个记号。

branches.en: A strong character is the mark of a settled nature.
branches.cn: 坚强的性格是稳定本性的记号。

branches.en: A story character is a figure stamped into fiction.
branches.cn: 故事人物是被压进虚构作品的形象。

branches.en: A character on a screen is the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 屏幕上的字符是最古老的字面义。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the idea of a distinguishing mark.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「识别记号」之上。

branches.en: A person's nature and a story figure share one word.
branches.cn: 人的本性与故事人物共用一个词。

intro.en: Character keeps the -character- stem in characteristic, characterize and characterless.
intro.cn: character 在 characteristic、characterize 与 characterless 中保留 -character- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter passed through Latin character into English with the mark intact.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 经拉丁语 character 进入英语，刻痕意象完好保留。

items.example: Critics characterize the style as spare.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把这种风格描述为简省。

items.meaning: the way a figure is drawn

latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakter 指硬币上的印记。
拉丁语 character 保留了这一记号。

definition_en: a quality that is typical of a person or thing, or being typical of a particular group
core_image: 一个人身上反复出现、可以辨认的记号
scene: 这种鸟的尾羽比身体长得多。A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
sceneCN: 这里 characteristic 指「特有的；典型的」（第 2 个义项：某类事物明显具有的）；句意是长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。

senses.title: A typical feature
senses.definition: a quality that is typical of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物典型的品质
senses.example: Patience is her best characteristic.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她最突出的特点。
senses.why: The Greek adjective meant able to mark, so a characteristic is what marks a thing out.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语形容词意为能留下记号，因此特征是使某物得以辨识的记号。

senses.title: Typical of a group
senses.definition: being a typical quality of a particular person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物典型性质的
senses.example: A long tail is characteristic of the male bird.
senses.exampleCN: 长尾是这种雄鸟的典型特征。
senses.why: The same adjective says that a mark belongs to a whole kind, not just one member.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词说明这个记号属于整个类别，而不只是某一个成员。

intro.en: Characteristic is the Greek adjective of marking, built on the same stem as character.
intro.cn: characteristic 是希腊语中表示「留下记号」的形容词，与 character 同词干。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Kharakteristikos meant skilled at marking or distinctive.
items.cn: kharakteristikos 意为善于留下记号或有辨识度的。

items.en: Latin character and its adjective passed into scholarly use.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 及其形容词进入学术用语。

items.en: English characteristic named a distinguishing quality.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 characteristic 指有区分作用的品质。

items.en: The word now works as both a noun and an adjective.
items.cn: 如今该词既作名词也作形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists feature words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出表示特征的词。

entries.definition: to describe the nature of something
in a way that is typical
a particular quality of a person
showing the usual qualities of a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the phrase be characteristic of and the noun ending -istic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、短语 be characteristic of 以及名词化词尾 -istic。

normal.en: Characteristic is the adjective of character, so it describes the mark a thing leaves.
normal.cn: characteristic 是 character 的形容词，因此描述事物留下的记号。

normal.en: Be characteristic of means the quality belongs to the whole kind.
normal.cn: be characteristic of 意为这种品质属于整个类别。

normal.en: A defining characteristic is the mark that decides identity.
normal.cn: a defining characteristic 是决定身份的那道记号。

normal.en: The adverb characteristically adds -ally to the same stem.
normal.cn: 副词 characteristically 是在同一词干后加 -ally。

normal.en: The plural characteristics names several marks at once.
normal.cn: 复数 characteristics 一次指出好几道记号。

abstract.en: Picture a bird with a tail far longer than its body.
abstract.cn: 想象一只尾巴远长于身体的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint that identifies one person only.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚只认出一个人的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a list of family traits passed down the years.
abstract.cn: 想象一份代代相传的家族特征清单。

examples.en: The two species share several characteristics.
examples.cn: 这两个物种共有若干特征。

examples.en: Patience is characteristic of a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师的典型特征。

examples.en: Her style is characteristic of the period.
examples.cn: 她的风格是那个时期的典型风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: characteristic 是 character 加 -istic：一个人身上反复出现的记号，就是他的特征。

root: 源自希腊语 kharakteristikos（能留下记号的），与 character（刻痕）同词干，经拉丁语进入英语，指有辨识作用的品质。

sensesIntro.en: A mark that identifies a thing gives the noun a feature, and the same mark makes the adjective mean typical.
sensesIntro.cn: 辨识事物的记号给出名词「特征」，同一记号使形容词表示「典型的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark that tells one kind from another.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一类事物与另一类区分开的记号。

branches.en: Patience as a characteristic is a repeated mark.
branches.cn: 作为特征的耐心是一道反复出现的记号。

branches.en: A long tail marks the whole male group.
branches.cn: 长尾标记出整个雄性群体。

branches.en: Physical characteristics are marks you can observe.
branches.cn: 身体特征是可以观察到的记号。

branches.en: The noun names the mark, the adjective says it fits the kind.
branches.cn: 名词指那道记号，形容词说它契合该类。

branches.en: Be characteristic of links one mark to a whole class.
branches.cn: be characteristic of 把一道记号连到整个类别。

intro.en: Characteristic adds -istic to the character stem, and the adverb adds -ally.
intro.cn: characteristic 在 character 词干后加 -istic，副词再加 -ally。

latinIntro.en: Greek kharakter and kharakteristikos are the mark and the marking adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 与 kharakteristikos 分别是记号与「留下记号」的形容词。

items.example: The characteristic is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个特征很容易看出来。
寒冷的冬天是该地区的特点。

items.example: The nose is a useful feature.
items.exampleCN: 鼻子是有用的辨识部位。

latinEntries.example: Kharakter is the root of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakter 是这一词族的根。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 能留下记号或作区分的
latinEntries.exampleCN: kharakteristikos 演变为 characteristic。

definition_zh: n. 木炭；炭笔；炭画；深灰色
definition_en: a black fuel made by burning wood without air; a stick of it used for drawing
core_image: 炉底一层发光后变黑的炭块
scene: 炉子里还剩一层未燃尽的木炭。A layer of charcoal still glowed in the stove.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：charcoal 指木炭；句意是炉里还剩一层未燃尽的木炭。

senses.title: The black fuel
senses.definition: a black porous fuel made by heating wood without air
senses.definitionCN: 隔绝空气加热木材制成的黑色多孔燃料
senses.example: They cooked over charcoal all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整晚用木炭做饭。
senses.why: The word joins char, to turn, with coal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「转动」的 char 与 coal 组合。

senses.title: The drawing stick
senses.definition: a stick of charred wood used to draw, or a drawing made with it
senses.definitionCN: 用于绘画的炭条，或炭画作品
senses.example: The sketch is charcoal on rough paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅速写是粗纸上的炭笔画。
senses.why: Artists adopted the fuel as a drawing tool.
senses.whyCN: 画家把这种燃料当成绘画工具。

intro.en: Charcoal is literally charred coal, wood turned black in a sealed pit.
intro.cn: charcoal 字面就是「烧过的煤」，即封闭坑中烧黑的木头。

items.en: Charcole names wood burned in a pit.
items.cn: 中古英语 charcole 指坑中烧制的木炭。

items.en: The spelling settles as charcoal.
items.cn: 十六世纪拼写固定为 charcoal。

items.en: Charcoal burns hot with little smoke.
items.cn: 十七世纪木炭热而少烟。

items.en: Artists draw with sticks of charcoal.
items.cn: 十八世纪画家用炭条作画。

items.en: Charcoal filters and forges spread.
items.cn: 十九世纪木炭用于过滤与锻造。

items.en: Charcoal also names a deep grey.
items.cn: 现代也指深灰色。

note.en: The look-alike group takes pieces of the word; the near-meaning group ranks black fuels and residues.
note.cn: 形近组拆用了这个词的两半；近义组排列黑色燃料与残渣。

entries.definition: A small glowing piece of coal.

normalIntro.en: Wood turned black in a sealed pit becomes fuel and pencil at once.
normalIntro.cn: 土坑里焖黑的木头，既是燃料也是画笔。

normal.en: Char means to turn black.
normal.cn: char 意为烧黑。

normal.en: Coal is the black fuel.

definition_en: to ask a price for goods or services, to accuse someone officially, or to put electrical energy into a battery
core_image: 货物被装上马车，账单也随之压上来
scene: 前台递来一张账单。They charge extra for a room with a view.
sceneCN: 这里 charge 指「收费」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务索要钱款）；句意是带景观的房间他们要另外收费。

senses.title: To ask for money
senses.definition: to ask a price for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为商品或服务索要价款
senses.example: They charge extra for a room with a view.
senses.exampleCN: 带景观的房间他们要另外收费。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to load a cart, and loading a price onto a bill repeats the same image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为往车上装货，把价钱压到账单上重复了同一意象。

senses.title: To accuse formally
senses.definition: to accuse someone officially of a crime or fault
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯有罪行或过错
senses.example: The police charged him with theft.
senses.exampleCN: 警方指控他盗窃。
senses.why: Blame too could be loaded onto a person, so the cart metaphor gave the legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 罪责也能被压到一个人身上，于是装车的比喻给出了法律义。

senses.title: To put power into a battery
senses.definition: to put electrical energy into a battery or device
senses.definitionCN: 把电能送入电池或设备
senses.example: Charge the phone before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前把手机充好电。
senses.why: Electricity is loaded into a cell the way goods were loaded into a cart.
senses.whyCN: 电被装进电池，正如货物曾被装进马车。

intro.en: Charge goes back to a Latin verb for loading a cart, and every sense keeps something being loaded.
intro.cn: charge 可追溯到拉丁语表示装车的动词，每个义项都保留「装载某物」的意象。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a wagon or cart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carricare 意为往货车或马车上装货。

items.en: Caricare extended the verb to loading in general.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 caricare 把该动词扩展到一般意义的装载。

items.en: Chargier meant to load, burden or entrust.
items.cn: chargier 意为装载、使负担或托付。

items.en: English charge covered loading, burdening and ordering.
items.cn: 英语 charge 涵盖装载、使负担与命令。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a price, a legal accusation and electric power.
items.cn: 该词获得费用、法律指控与电能等义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charge stem, while the meaning group lists accusing and loading words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charge 词干，近义组列出指控与装载类词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the loading cart, the phrase in charge of and the battery sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用装货的马车、短语 in charge of 以及电池义。

normal.en: Charge and car share the Latin loading verb, since a cart is what gets loaded.
normal.cn: charge 与 car 共享拉丁语装车动词，因为被装的就是车。

normal.en: In charge of means the duty has been loaded onto you.
normal.cn: in charge of 意为责任被压到了你身上。

normal.en: Charge a fee is loading a price onto the customer.

normal.en: Charge the battery is loading power instead of goods.
normal.cn: charge the battery 是装电而不是装货。

normal.en: Free of charge means no load of cost at all.
normal.cn: free of charge 意为完全不用承担费用的重负。

abstract.en: Picture a cart piled high until the wheels bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车堆得高高的，轮子都压弯了。

abstract.en: Picture a phone plugged in and glowing at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一部插着电、边缘发亮的手机。

abstract.en: Picture a guard pointing at a man in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象警卫在法庭上指着一个人。

examples.en: The garage charges too much for repairs.
examples.cn: 这家修车厂收费太高。

examples.en: She was charged with careless driving.
examples.cn: 她被指控粗心驾驶。

examples.en: The nurse in charge of the ward was kind.
examples.cn: 负责病房的护士很和善。

sensesIntro.en: Loading goods gives a price, loading blame gives an accusation, and loading power gives the battery sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 装货给出价钱，装罪责给出指控，装电力给出充电义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods piled onto a cart.

branches.en: A price is a load placed on the buyer.

branches.en: An accusation loads blame onto a person.

branches.en: Charging a battery loads it with power.

intro.en: Charge keeps the -charg- stem in charger, discharge and chargeable.
intro.cn: charge 在 charger、discharge 与 chargeable 中保留 -charg- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin carricare and Late Latin caricare are the loading verbs behind charge.

definition_en: a device that puts electricity into a battery; an old word for a war horse
core_image: 插头接上墙，指示灯变红
scene: 手机没电了，他从包里翻出充电器。His phone died, so he dug the charger out of his bag.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：charger 指充电器；句意是手机没电，他从包里翻出充电器。

senses.title: The power device
senses.definition: a device that supplies electricity to recharge a battery
senses.definitionCN: 给电池充电的供电装置
senses.example: The charger is still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 充电器还在车里。
senses.why: The device charges a battery in the old sense of loading it.
senses.whyCN: 这个装置按 charge 古老的「装填」义给电池装载电量。

senses.title: A war horse
senses.definition: an old word for a horse ridden into battle
senses.definitionCN: 指载人上阵的战马的旧词
senses.example: The knight calmed his charger.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士安抚他的战马。
senses.why: A charger carried a rider loaded for war.
senses.whyCN: 战马载着全副武装的骑手。

intro.en: Charger is charge plus -er; charge itself came from a Latin verb for loading a cart.
intro.cn: charger 是 charge 加 -er；charge 本身来自拉丁语「装车」的动词。

definition_zh: n. 个人魅力，领袖气质；（神学）神赐的恩典
definition_en: a strong personal quality that attracts devotion; in theology, a gift freely given by God
core_image: 一个人开口，满屋的人都抬头
scene: 他一开口，整间屋子就被他的魅力镇住了。When he spoke, the room was held by his charisma.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：charisma 指个人魅力；句意是他一开口，整屋人都被他的魅力镇住。

senses.title: Personal magnetism
senses.definition: a strong personal quality that makes others follow or admire
senses.definitionCN: 使他人追随或倾慕的强烈个人特质
senses.example: Her charisma filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的魅力充满整个大厅。
senses.why: Greek kharisma meant a free gift of grace.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kharisma 指白白赐予的恩典。

senses.title: A divine gift
senses.definition: a gift believed to be given freely by God
senses.definitionCN: 被认为由神白白赐予的恩赐
senses.example: The letter lists the charismata of the early church.
senses.exampleCN: 书信列出了早期教会的各样恩赐。
senses.why: The theological sense came first in English.
senses.whyCN: 在英语中神学含义先出现。

intro.en: Charisma comes from Greek kharisma, a free gift, from kharis, grace.
intro.cn: charisma 来自希腊语 kharisma（白得的礼物），源自 kharis（恩典）。

items.en: Kharis means grace or favour.
items.cn: kharis 意为恩典、恩惠。

items.en: Kharisma means a free gift.
items.cn: kharisma 意为白得的礼物。

items.en: Latin keeps charisma for a spiritual gift.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 charisma 指属灵恩赐。

items.en: English uses charisma for gifts of grace.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语指恩典的恩赐。

items.en: Charisma comes to mean personal appeal.
items.cn: 二十世纪转为个人吸引力。

items.en: The everyday sense now leads.
items.cn: 现代以日常义为主。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the char- sound; the near-meaning group names kinds of attraction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 char- 的读音；近义组列出不同类型的吸引力。

normalIntro.en: A free gift of grace became the power to draw a room.
normalIntro.cn: 白白赐下的恩典，变成了吸引满屋人的力量。

normal.en: A leader with charisma is followed.

abstract.en: A room bending toward one voice.

abstract.en: A gift that asks for followers.

examples.en: The coach had charisma but no plan.

examples.en: Charisma alone cannot run a government.
examples.cn: 单靠魅力治理不了政府。

examples.en: His charisma drew a crowd at every stop.
examples.cn: 他的魅力在每一站都聚起人群。

sensesIntro.cn: 神学上的恩典之礼，变成了日常的吸引力。

definition_en: kindness shown to others, an organization that helps people in need, or money and goods given to them
core_image: 一只手把面包递到另一只伸出的手里
scene: 教堂门口摆着一只募捐箱。The charity provides meals for homeless families.
sceneCN: 这里 charity 指「慈善机构」（第 2 个义项：从事救济的组织）；句意是这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。

senses.title: Kindness toward others
senses.definition: kindness and understanding shown to other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与体谅
senses.example: She treats everyone with charity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对每个人都心怀善意。
senses.why: Latin caritas meant dearness and Christian love, the warm root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caritas 意为珍爱与基督之爱，是这个词温暖的根。

senses.title: An organization that helps
senses.definition: an organization set up to help people in need
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助困难者而设立的组织
senses.example: The charity provides meals for homeless families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供餐食。
senses.why: A body of people organized for love of neighbours took the name of the love itself.
senses.whyCN: 一群为关爱邻人而组织起来的人，借用了这份关爱本身的名字。

senses.title: Money or aid given
senses.definition: money or goods given to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 给予困难者的钱款或物品
senses.example: He gave his spare coat to charity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把多余的外套捐给了慈善机构。
senses.why: The abstract love became concrete in the coins and clothes actually handed over.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的仁爱在真正交出的钱币与衣物中变得具体。

intro.en: Charity descends from a Latin word for dearness, which early Christian writers used for love of one's neighbours.
intro.cn: charity 源自拉丁语表示珍爱的词，早期基督教作家用它指对邻人的爱。

items.en: Carus meant dear or precious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、亲爱的。

items.en: Caritas meant dearness and, in Christian use, loving kindness.
items.cn: caritas 意为珍爱，在基督教用法中指仁爱。

items.en: Charité carried both love and almsgiving.
items.cn: charité 同时带有爱与施舍之意。

items.en: English charity named Christian love and mercy.
items.cn: 英语 charity 指基督之爱与怜悯。

items.en: The word now also names the groups and gifts that express this love.
items.cn: 如今该词也指表达这份爱的组织与捐赠。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charitable stem, while the meaning group lists kindness and aid words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charitable 词干，近义组列出善意与援助类词。
